entries.name: UCSF ChimeraX
entries.vendor: UCSF Resource for Biocomputing, Visualization, and Informatics (RBVI)

licence.name: UC Regents non-commercial licence; separate paid commercial licence priced by user count

engines.name: OpenGL scene renderer
engines.does: Draws atoms, bonds, cartoons, surfaces and maps through OpenGL; triangle counts per atom, bond and ribbon are tunable, and an off-screen path renders images and movie frames at any size.

engines.name: Key light and ambient shadow engine
engines.does: Renders a shadow map for one key light and a set of up to 1024 ambient shadow directions, the second giving an ambient-occlusion look without ray tracing.

engines.name: Movie encoder
engines.does: Records frames to image files, then encodes them with ffmpeg into several video containers.

engines.name: Surface and map engines
engines.does: Computes solvent-excluded and Gaussian surfaces from atoms and contours or slices volume data such as cryo-EM maps.

capabilities.does: The surface command wraps chosen atoms in a solvent-excluded surface; probeRadius (default 1.4 A), gridSpacing and enclose/include control smoothness and which atoms share one envelope; patches keep links to their atoms.
capabilities.inputs: atom spec; probeRadius; gridSpacing; enclose; include
capabilities.outputs: surface model, coloured per atom patch

capabilities.does: Giving a resolution value to surface builds an isosurface of summed atom Gaussians instead; level sets the contour and gridSpacing defaults to a tenth of the resolution.

Edit operations on surfaces: dust hides small blobs, zone keeps parts near chosen atoms, smooth relaxes the mesh, splitbycolor makes one model per colour, cap toggles caps on clipped surfaces, style switches solid, mesh or dot.
capabilities.inputs: surface model; distance, size, factor, iterations

capabilities.does: cartoon style sets ribbon width and thickness, cross-section (oval, rectangle, barbell), sides, divisions per residue and strand arrowheads; helices can be drawn as ribbon, tube, cylinder or wrapped tube.
capabilities.inputs: residue spec; width, thickness, xsection, sides, modeHelix

capabilities.does: cartoon byattribute (worm) makes the ribbon radius follow a per-residue value such as B-factor, giving a putty-like tube.
cartoon tether draws connectors between the ribbon and atoms that sit off the ribbon path; shape (cone, steeple, cylinder), sides, scale and opacity are settable.
style switches atoms between sphere (full van der Waals), stick and ball-and-stick; ringFill fills aromatic rings thick or thin; dashes sets pseudobond dash count.

lighting presets named simple, default, full, soft, gentle and flat set light mixes at once; full adds key-light shadows and 64-direction ambient shadows, flat uses ambient light only with silhouettes.
multiShadow N sets how many directions form the ambient shadows (0 off, up to 1024); msMapSize and msDepthBias tune the depth maps and self-shadowing offset.
Key light has direction, intensity and colour, a separate fill light, and optional shadow map with quality coarse to finer (1024 to 8192 pixels) and a depthBias against self-shadowing.
depthCue fades colours toward a chosen colour between depthCueStart and depthCueEnd, given as fractions of the distance from front to back clip plane.
graphics silhouettes draws outlines at borders and depth jumps; colour, pixel width and the depth jump threshold (fraction of clip range, default 0.03) are settable.
graphics quality scales triangle counts for atoms, bonds and ribbons, or fixes them (atomTriangles, bondTriangles, bondSides, ribbonDivisions) with caps near 5 million triangles each.
graphics rate reports frames per second and sets a target (maxFrameRate default 60) and optional vertical sync.
clip activates near and far planes fixed to the screen and front and back planes fixed to the scene, with offsets from a position, an axis, a coordinate system and per-model switches.
capabilities.inputs: plane name; offset; position; axis; coordinateSystem

capabilities.does: camera selects mono perspective, orthographic, side-by-side, top-bottom or sequential stereo, 360-degree equirectangular (also stereo) and 180-degree dome projection with fieldOfView and eyeSeparation.

movie record then movie encode capture frames and write h264 (mp4), webm, ogv, mov, avi, wmv or animated PNG; supersample, size, framerate, quality, bitrate and roundTrip loops are options; crossfade and duplicate insert transitions.
capabilities.inputs: frame sequence; format, size, supersample, framerate

capabilities.does: perframe runs a command each display frame with $1-style placeholders filled from a range or the frame counter; frames, interval and zero-padded formats allow turns, fades and numbered image saves.
view name stores camera, clip planes and model positions; view <name> N frames then moves between two saved views, rotating the camera linearly in angle and interpolating moved models.

morph builds a trajectory between two or more aligned models; corkscrew (default) or linear rigid-body paths, internal-coordinate or Cartesian interpolation, and a rate curve (linear, ramp, sinusoidal) are choices.
capabilities.inputs: models in order; frames; method; rate; cartesian

capabilities.does: coordset plays or jumps through trajectory frames by start,end,step; pauseFrames slows playback, loop and bounce repeat it, holdSteady stabilises chosen atoms and computeSs refreshes secondary structure each frame.

Atom specs nest model (#), chain (/), residue (:) and atom (@) levels with ranges, wildcards, built-in names (protein, ligand, helix), attribute tests (@@bfactor>40), zones by distance and &, |, ~ operators.

color paints by element, chain, polymer, nucleotide base, sequence position (rainbow) or any numeric attribute with named or custom palettes (rainbow, red-white-blue, ColorBrewer, alphafold, pae); target letters pick atoms, cartoons or surfaces.

Surfaces can take colour from a map value (sample, electrostatic with default offset 1.4 A, gradient), from radial, cylindrical or height distance, from nearby atoms (color zone) or from a texture image.
capabilities.inputs: surface; map or axis; palette; range

capabilities.does: volume shows maps as isosurface, mesh or image (semi-transparent cloud), single plane, orthoplanes or tilted slab; level can be absolute, in standard deviations or RMS; step, region and appearance presets control sampling and look.

volume zone limits a map to a radius around atoms, volume mask cuts it to a surface, volume gaussian smooths or sharpens it, and volume tile lays slices side by side; the page also lists add, resample and scale operations.

measure reports surface area, enclosed volume, solvent-accessible area (sasa), buried area between sets, contact area, convexity, inertia axes, map statistics, map-model values, correlation and map symmetry type.

alphafold fetch, match and search retrieve database models; they are coloured by pLDDT in four bands, PAE plots and PAE-coloured contact lines are available, and predictions can be superposed on an open chain.
2dlabels places text and arrows in screen space with colour, background colour, size, font, bold, italic, margin, outline and position as fractions of the window; visibility can fade over frames.

save writes the whole scene, ignoring clipping, as glTF (.glb), STL, OBJ, X3D, VRML or VTK. For glTF, preserveTransparency (default true) keeps transparency and flatLighting drops normals so triangles look faceted. OBJ output carries no colours.
save writes PNG, TIFF, JPEG, GIF, BMP or PPM from an off-screen render with width, height or pixelSize, supersample (default 3), JPEG quality and transparentBackground for PNG and TIFF.
A .cxs session file stores models, selections, named views, scenes, aliases, attributes and the log; maps are skipped unless includeMaps is set.
The programming manual documents a Python API, C++ libraries and bundles (installable packages); commands, tools and file formats are added as bundles.

outcomes: publication figures with silhouettes and ambient shadows

rea.notes: Licensing page says non-commercial use is free after accepting an agreement and that commercial use needs a separate licence; that agreement (redistribution and reverse-engineering terms) was not opened. Full command manual and Python API reference are public; source availability is described in the programming manual but was not verified here.

entries.name: PyMOL
entries.vendor: Schrodinger, LLC (open-source core; Incentive PyMOL sold as a supported build)

licence.name: BSD-like licence for the open-source repository; a supported Incentive build is sold separately

engines.name: Built-in ray tracer
engines.does: Renders final images offline from the scene; ray_trace_mode adds outline or cartoon-style looks, and angle and shift arguments make matched stereo pairs.

engines.name: POV-Ray bridge
engines.does: The ray command can hand the scene to an external POV-Ray install instead of the built-in tracer (renderer argument 1).

engines.name: OpenGL shader viewer
engines.does: Interactive display, including volume rendering done with shaders and no ray tracing.

capabilities.does: ray takes width, height, a renderer choice (default, internal, POV-Ray) and angle/shift for stereo pairs; zero size means the window size; orthoscopic and field_of_view set the projection.

ray_trace_mode 0 gives plain colour, 1 colour with black outline, 2 outline only (line-art look), 3 quantised colour with outline; ray_trace_color sets the outline colour and ray_trace_trans_cutoff skips faint transparency.
png writes the view at a pixel or physical size (inch or cm suffix with dpi) and can ray trace first (ray=1); setting ray_opaque_background to 0 gives a transparent background.
light_count sets the number of light sources (default 2); 0 or 1 removes the directional light and with it shadows, and the number also changes ambient lighting.

The settings list names further ray-tracer controls: ray_shadow, ray_trace_fog, ray_trace_gain, ray_trace_disco_factor, ray_texture, ray_direct_shade and ray_blend colours; their effects were not read from their own pages.
Selections combine property keywords (chain, resi, resn, name, elem, ss, b, q), classes (organic, solvent, polymer, backbone, metals), and, or and not, plus byres, bychain and bymolecule expansion.
Distance operators: within X of, around X, expand X, near_to X of, beyond X of, gap X, plus bond-based bound_to, neighbor and extend N, and matching with in and like.

spectrum colours along a palette (rainbow default, blue_red, blue_white_red, red_yellow_green or a colour list) by count, partial charge, B-factor or any iterate expression, with min, max and per-residue options.
isosurface and isomesh build a contour object from a map at a level, optionally limited to a selection plus buffer and carved to a radius around atoms; the result can be loaded as a new state.
capabilities.inputs: map object; level; selection; buffer; carve

capabilities.does: volume turns a map into a volume object coloured through a named ramp; opacity follows the ramp, it is shader-based without ray tracing, and multiple volumes do not blend correctly.
clip moves near and far planes, shifts the whole slab, sets slab thickness around a selection, or clips to a buffer around chosen atoms.

scene stores and recalls named scenes that capture view, enabled objects, colours, representations and the frame index; transitions between scenes are interpolated and can be driven by mdo during a movie.
capabilities.inputs: scene key; flags view, color, rep, active, frame

capabilities.does: mview stores camera or per-object keyframes and interpolates between them (store, clear, interpolate, reinterpolate, toggle, smooth); power slows motion at a keyframe and freeze stops automatic reinterpolation.
mset maps molecular states to movie frames with repeat (x) and range (-) operators; madd appends to an existing movie, and one-to-one mapping plays a trajectory.

save writes selected atoms to a file and picks the format from the suffix. The page lists .pdb, .pqr, .mol, .sdf, .mol2, .pov, .obj/.mtl, .wrl, .idtf, .dae, .png, .pse, .psw, .aln and .fasta. A .pse suffix saves the whole session; .aln writes CLUSTALW alignments.
surface_quality is an integer that sets how finely surface polygons are sampled; higher values (2 to 4) look better for publication but take much longer to compute and ray trace.

Cartoon settings include cartoon_sampling, oval length and width, rect length and width, loop and helix radius, fancy and flat sheets, dumbbell sizes, putty radius, scale min and max and transform, nucleic acid mode, transparency.
Size settings for atom representations include stick_radius, stick_ball and ball ratio, sphere_scale, sphere_quality, sphere_mode, line_width and ribbon_width.
The settings list contains depth_cue, fog and fog_start, which control fading with distance in the viewer.
Every command has a Python form (cmd.mset, cmd.clip and so on), so a session can be scripted from PyMOL command files or from Python.
The community wiki hosts a plugin category, a plugin tutorial and a script library, with examples such as PySSA, CavitOmiX and MOLE.

rea.restrictions: The README says the open-source project uses a BSD-like licence (full text in a LICENSE file that was not opened).
rea.notes: Several pymolwiki pages (Surface, Cartoon, Mset detail) returned server errors during this sweep, so surface-type and mset coverage is thin.

entries.name: Mol* (Molstar)
entries.vendor: Mol* contributors (started by PDBe and RCSB PDB)

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: WebGL renderer
engines.does: Draws structures, surfaces and volumes in the browser with GLSL shaders, written in TypeScript.

engines.name: BinaryCIF codec
engines.does: Compressed binary form of mmCIF that is decoded and streamed so large structures load over limited bandwidth.

engines.name: Mesoscale renderer
engines.does: Instanced rendering with sphere impostors, level of detail and culling for models with up to billions of atoms.

engines.name: Gaussian surface generator
engines.does: Builds Gaussian and molecular surface meshes from atoms for display.

capabilities.does: Representations named in the paper: cartoon and ribbon, balls-and-sticks, lines, points, Gaussian surface, Gaussian volume and molecular surface, with labelled ligands and 3D symbols for glycans.
Colour themes work from atom properties (occupancy, uncertainty), residue properties (hydrophobicity, accessible surface), chain identity and annotations such as wwPDB validation report quality.
Lighting styles are matte, metallic, glossy and plastic; the paper also lists outlines, fog and screen-space ambient occlusion that darkens crevices.
Screen-space ambient occlusion is applied in the viewer; the mesoscale app adds a multiscale variant and screen-space contact shadows.
Outlines are available; the paper compares them with ambient occlusion and with direct plus ambient light, giving an illustration look.
Fog or depth cueing fades distant parts of the scene.
Electron density and cryo-EM maps are shown as isosurface or volume; supported map formats are CCP4/MRC/MAP, DSN6/BRIX, CUBE, DX and BinaryCIF density.
capabilities.inputs: map file or density server data

capabilities.does: Trajectories (XTC, TRR, DCD, NCTRAJ) load next to a structure or topology file (PSF, PRMTOP, TOP) and play as animation.

Streaming BinaryCIF and a tuned renderer let ribosomes, capsids and cellPACK models display interactively; the two figures of the paper give different sizes for its cellPACK HIV model (about 68 million atoms in one, over 13 million in another).

Mesoscale Explorer stores each molecule once and draws copies by position and rotation, uses ray-cast sphere impostors, distance level of detail and frustum and occlusion culling, with Ultra to Performance quality presets.
capabilities.inputs: manifest of entities and instance transforms

capabilities.does: Front and back clip planes move with Shift plus the mouse wheel (or a settings slider), and focusing an object adjusts them automatically.
The mesoscale app applies plane, sphere, cube, cylinder and infinite-cone clipping objects to selected subsets of a scene.
Snapshots store camera, clipping, colour and visibility; the viewer interpolates between them, 3D labels can link to snapshots, and guided tours chain them with Markdown text.

Selection mode plus a paint-brush tool applies a preset or custom colour to a selection; a component menu colours by chain ID, hydrophobicity or secondary structure; annotation presets use validation or assembly symmetry data.
The same selection tool sets transparency on a 0 to 100 slider; the background colour can be solid or transparent.
Clicking a residue focuses it, shows its neighbours as ball-and-stick and draws local non-covalent interactions; clicking it again hides the surroundings.
A .molj state file links to the original data and a .molx file bundles the data; both can open from a local file or a remote location.

MolViewSpec describes a scene as a tree of nodes (download, parse, structure, component, representation, color, label, tooltip, camera, focus, canvas); MVSJ is JSON, MVSX a zip with referenced files; volumes and primitives are supported.
Loads mmCIF and coreCIF (including BinaryCIF), GRO, MOL, MOL2, PDB and PDBQT, SDF and XYZ structures, and PLY triangle meshes as shapes.
Companion tools serve model data, volume data and plugin state, and a command-line converter turns CIF into BinaryCIF.
Mol* is an npm package and plugin framework; PDBe-Molstar (JS plugin and web component) and RCSB Mol* embed it in other sites with helper methods for control.

Plugin code selects atoms with MolScript builder queries (MS.struct.generator.atomGroups with chain-test and residue-test, MS.core.rel.eq and inRange, combinator.merge), compiled id-range strings, or StructureElement schema objects, then converts results to loci for focus and highlight.

Canvas3D settings are read from plugin.canvas3d.props.renderer and written with PluginCommands.Canvas3D.SetSettings; backgroundColor, highlightColor and selectColor are set this way and camera.manualReset keeps the view when representations are added.
An Interactions extension computes or accepts custom interactions between selections or structures; the page defers details to example source code.
A screenshot and state-snapshot tool captures the current view with resolution options and a download.

outcomes: interactive web viewers for PDB and AlphaFold entries
screenshots with outlines and ambient occlusion

entries.name: cellPACK
entries.vendor: Autin, Johnson, Olson and colleagues (Scripps); current repository under the mesoscope organisation, hosted run at Allen Institute for Cell Science

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: Grid-based packing engine
engines.does: Divides the container volume into a grid for collision checks; ingredients explore continuous space inside voxels, and harder ingredients are placed first.

engines.name: Placement methods
engines.does: Two place methods exist, jitter (random trial placements) and spheresSST (sphere-based), chosen per object or globally.

engines.name: Gradient engine
engines.does: Biases where ingredients land using x, y, z, vector, radial or surface gradients with falloff curves.

capabilities.does: The pack command takes a recipe (-r) and optional config (-c); recipes list objects and a composition of counts; the modern v2 schema has objects, gradients and composition with inheritance, and v1 is the legacy schema.

Each recipe object has a type: mesh, grow, a single-shape primitive (single_sphere, single_cube, single_cylinder) or a multi-part one (multi_sphere, multi_cylinder). Radius and RGB colour (0 to 1) are set per object. A mesh takes path, name, format and coordinate_system (left or right, default left).

place_method is jitter or spheresSST; jitter_attempts (default 5) and max_jitter (per-axis, in grid units, default 1,1,1) shape the random trials; a config can force one method everywhere (overwrite_place_method).
packing_mode selects random, close, closePartner, randomPartner, gradient, hexatile, squaretile or triangletile arrangements for an object.

Gradients have a mode (x, y, z, vector, radial, surface of a mesh), a pick_mode (max, min, rnd, linear, binary, sub, reg), a weight falloff (linear, square, cube, power, exponential with decay_length), plus reversed and invert.
Partners list objects that attract or repel an ingredient, with probability_binding (default 0.5), relative positions, excluded_names, probability_repelled and a weight (default 0.2).

Composition nests containers and puts counts of objects into interior, surface, inner-leaflet or outer-leaflet regions, with a priority that orders packing; available_regions limits where an object may go.
A whole recipe can serve as an ingredient inside a larger one, for example an HIV particle inside blood plasma; ingredient priority orders harder objects first.
Fibres and branched filaments (von Willebrand factor, actin, DNA, lipopolysaccharide) grow from seeds inside the container.
randomness_seed fixes the random sequence, number_of_packings repeats independent runs, bounding_box sets the volume (default 100 per side) and version tags the output name.
Config options cover the collision grid: inner_grid_method (trimesh or raytrace), saving and loading a grid file, cleaning the cache, spacing, and use_periodicity for periodic boundaries.
The default output format is simularium; image_export_options set hollow rendering, projection axis (default z) and voxel size for image output.
Analysis options save extra results and plots; the paper describes position and orientation histograms, available-volume graphs by probe size and nearest-neighbour distance export.
Through the uPy layer the paper lists plugins for PMV, Cinema 4D, Maya and Blender and a result reader for UCSF Chimera.
Results and recipes can be stored in AWS or Firestore, uploaded to S3, opened in a browser, and packed in parallel when configured.

outcomes: input for web or DCC viewers

engines.does: Built-in ray-tracing renderer used for final images; scenes can also go to POV-Ray and RenderMan.

capabilities.does: Each molecule is drawn as a set of representations. Every representation combines an atom selection, a drawing method, a colouring method and a material that sets shininess and opacity.
Scenes export to external renderers such as POV-Ray, RenderMan and Tachyon for ray-traced stills and frames.
Embedded Tcl and Python interpreters run user scripts; Tcl/Tk also lets VMD talk to other programs.
A plugin collection adds analysis and building tools such as electrostatic forces, RMSD, SASA and QM/ONIOM, with a plugin browser.
Works with molecular, volumetric and sequence data and arbitrary graphics objects in one scene.
Supports interactive molecular dynamics with NAMD; early versions added CAVE virtual-environment and haptic input.

entries.name: NGL Viewer

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: WebGL renderer
engines.does: Draws molecules in the browser through WebGL.

capabilities.does: Structures can be shown with several combined representations. The manual covers 22 types: cartoon, surface, licorice, spacefill, hyperball, ball+stick, line, point, label, distance, contact, validation, axes, unitcell, base, backbone, trace, tube, ribbon, rocket, rope, helixorient. Most take colour and radius options.
The surface representation takes surfaceType vws, sas, ms, ses or av and a probeRadius, so van der Waals, accessible and excluded surfaces are all available.
Cartoon, rope and tube styles expose subdiv, radialSegments, tension, capped, wireframe and aspectRatio; rope adds smooth.
The contact representation draws polar or polar-backbone contacts filtered by maxDistance and maxAngle.
Colour schemes include element, chainid, residueindex, resname, sstruc, bfactor, hydrophobicity, occupancy, electrostatic, geoquality, densityfit, volume, value, random and uniform.

ColormakerRegistry.addScheme registers a function that returns a colour per atom; addSelectionScheme maps selection strings to colours with a catch-all default; both return an id used as the colour option.
A selection language picks atoms for representations and colouring, and mouse picking selects interactively.
Trajectories load as DCD with PSF, NCTRAJ with PRMTOP, or TRR/XTC with TOP, including remote streaming through MDSrv.
Density volumes in MRC/MAP/CCP4, DX/DXBIN, CUBE, BRIX/DSN6 and XPLOR/CNS formats can be displayed alongside structures.
The viewer can export the current view as an image.
Installs from npm or as one self-contained script and is driven by a JavaScript API; an examples folder holds a full GUI app.
